required_outcomes: Sends the landlord the tenant's report (kitchen extractor fan will not turn on) and asks whether he wants the agency to send its contractor or to use his own, as the landlord approval step requires.
Acknowledges the tenant (Clara) in writing: the report is logged and the landlord is being asked, without promising a visit date.
Records the wait for the landlord with a dated review or follow-up (about 3 days, as the job is routine).
acceptable_alternatives: Asking the tenant at the same time whether there is a wall switch or fused spur for the hood near the hob that might be off, as a quick check while the landlord is asked.
Asking the tenant for a photo of the hood and its controls, provided the landlord is still asked in this run.
positive_behaviours: Treats the job as routine (no safety risk is reported) and says so in the case record.
Mentions the photo the tenant referred to when forwarding the report, without describing its contents.
red_flags: Escalating a routine extractor-fan report to a human.
Treating the fan as an emergency or electrical hazard with nothing in the report to support it.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a contractor or returning the ticket to provider selection before the landlord has answered, with no standing instruction or spend limit on file.
Telling the tenant a contractor is booked or coming.
critical_failures: Ending the turn without asking the landlord for a decision and without telling the tenant anything, so the job stalls at intake.
